messages.subject: License Issue?
parts:

and your linking against their code.

Best

I don't see a problem with rApache's license.

Jeff

with the discussion of compatibility of the licenses. What you consider
to be desirable for the software you write may be different, so you can
craft various license exceptions, if it comes to that.

messages.author: 3ea57457192f4f3b
messages.subject: Re: License Issue?
parts: No copyrighted R source code is distributed with RApache either. Furthermore, in future, RApache can be linked to another implementation of the S language that is not GPL. So I don't think RApache is a derivative work of R per se. If it is, than every R package is also a derivative work, and should be GPL'd as well, which I don't think is the case.

messages.author: d2cfae0f18aa5a77
messages.subject: Re: License Issue?
parts:
IANAL too and I'm not related to FSF nor to ASF.

The GPL states that any project which links (statically or
dynamically) to a GPL'd library must be GPL'd too. No matter if you
might replace one implementation with another.

I agree with Jeroen that when it comes to R packages the situation
gets even worse. But I can't find a reliable source which provides an
answer to those questions.

I just wanted to point you to this (in my point of view) licensing
conflict. What if you license RApache under GPL? Would it violate the
GPL if you plug your mod into the non GPL httpd?

I'm curious if you find a solution...

Markus

messages.author: 417414441a0ca1d9
messages.subject: Re: License Issue?
parts:
On 12/16/2011 11:38 AM, Jeffrey Horner wrote:
>
> A solution? I'm not sure there's even a problem.

I don't think that's quite fair. True, you can't worry about every legal
eventuality out there, but you also want to be pretty comfortable that
Rapache is distributed under a license that means that an average person
can actually use it. I wonder if the Software Freedom Law Center can
advise on whether Rapache's license arrangement makes sense, or maybe
they can recommend someone else who could.

messages.author: 42eed4e1caba0ad0
messages.subject: Re: License Issue?
parts:
Jack, do you perhaps have one license in mind that will mend all this fuss about licensing, and make our lives easier? I agree with Jeff... I'm not sure that there's a problem, unless you represent interests of "The Big Ones" like Google, MS, etc. And I'm pretty sure that even if RApache was released under fully compatible license, "The Big Ones" would bring a bunch of clever lawyers who will prove the opposite and win the case. Either propose a solution, or just use it as is, for God sake... it's not like SWAT team will storm your apartment because of one Apache module... O_o

Well, I'm not the one that raised the issue in the first place. I'm not
even an active Rapache user today! (I was a user until recently, and I'm
still a huge fan.) If I were a user, I'd be OK with using Rapache as is.

My very naive, not-a-laywer, guess about this situation is that there
are two ways to resolve it: either seek the advice of SLFC or a similar
organization that exists for the very purpose of providing legal support
to free / open source projects, or release Rapache into the public domain.
